name: Bela
overview: Bela was a male member of the tribe of Reuben, identified specifically as the son of Azaz. His mention in Scripture is brief, with no additional notes recorded beyond his tribal affiliation and lineage. As a Reubenite, he is part of the descendants of Reuben, Jacob's firstborn son.
namesAndTitles: The name Bela means 'swallower' or 'devourer,' reflecting a proper name of Hebrew origin. This name was not given directly by God but is recorded in 1 Chronicles 5:7, providing insight into the meaning behind his personal designation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Bela was the son of Azaz. Additionally, it is inferred that Zechariah was his father, indicating a familial link within the Reubenite lineage. Beyond these relationships, no further family connections are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Bela's significance lies in his place within the genealogical records of the tribe of Reuben, emphasizing the continuity of God's covenant people through their descendants. His identification as the son of Azaz situates him within the broader narrative of Israel's tribes, underscoring the importance of lineage in maintaining the identity and heritage of God's chosen people.
